images.title: Write 132 in base 60
images.purpose: Shows writing a number in the base 60 place system: 132 is two 60s and 12, written 2 | 12.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A number at the top, a downward arrow, and two place boxes below.
images.exact_structure: Top centre, large: 132. One dark arrow points down. Below, two boxes side by side with thin dark outlines, headed in grey (#6B7280): 60s (left), 1s (right). The left box holds 2 in teal (#0072B2); the right box holds 12 in amber (#E69F00). Exactly 2 boxes. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Group into 60s and 1s and write each count in its own place.
images.description: Shows writing a number in the base 60 place system: 132 is two 60s and 12, written 2 | 12.
images.context: 132 = (2) × 60 + 12; other items 63, 200, 60 and 3605 use the same move, two with an empty place.

image_decisions.why: The practice concept's core move is placing the count of each power of 60 in its place.
